## Result

- Skill: delivery-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Package members: primary plan, docs/plans/2026-09-08-skill-model-proposal-family-pilot.md. Other subjects are governing or feasibility basis, not extra Delivery package members.
- Upstream review ID: design-review-r2, approved for the unchanged Skill/System and retained-source package.
- Review ID and round: delivery-review-r1, round 1.
- Traceability result: sufficient allocation of SKL-SR-01–23, SKL-DEC-01–05, the eight Design boundary dimensions and four composed hazards into M1/M2, TG-01–05 and TG-FINAL-01.
- Material findings: none.
- Correction targets: none.
- Recording status: recorded upon successful primary review-record persistence.
- Open blockers: none.
- Immediate next stage: isolated stop; return to route for any separately authorized continuation.
- Claim limitations: exact Delivery package approval only. No implementation, work initialization, milestone completion, source adoption, final review, Verify, publication or customer installation is established.

## Independence and exact basis

The parent authored the plan and upstream Design; the user supplied direction and correction requirements. Independent agent /root/independent_delivery_review authored none of those engineering contributions and made no changes to them. The reviewer read the entire exact primary plan, Skill's requirements, realization, source maps and acceptance boundaries, the scoped System composition changes, the approved upstream review, the resolved prior finding, relevant source-policy and production consumer excerpts, and plan-authoring evidence. Actual contributor separation supports this independent judgment.

Primary full scoped context is complete for selected activity, model, proposal, plan, review, finding, blocker, applicability, evidence and decision records. The registered plan identity is sha256:afe231f1bcd0a5a2afd189867f42e237916bdba8e670cdd53cfec26d431d0b39 and exact subject inspection matches it. Fresh inspection of 49 subjects finds no drift among the 35 subjects of design-review-r2. That approved review remains current, the original reporter resolved skl-dr-001, and there are no open selected blockers. The stale earlier review remains historical and is not reused as approval. Upstream detailed semantic assessment is relied on for its unchanged scope; this assessment independently judges the plan's allocation and proof feasibility.

## Sequencing and implementation readiness

M1 is a coherent rollback and review unit: the four named pilot content files move recording procedure only together with profile selection, installed placement, canonical regression checks and supported archive comparison. The current production validator returns no errors when the body heading is absent, installed placement uses the same heading to select v2, and the archive comparison extracts the old body section. The plan names all three actual consumers and requires negative production-boundary proof before relying on relocation. Unchanged assets, shared resources, non-pilot bodies and specialist responsibilities remain explicit preservation boundaries.

M2 depends on assessed M1 value and required concern disposition. It snapshots the four Design-selected originals before replacing mapped common prose, retains mixed plan/method authority and operational inputs, and reconciles governance/current consumers as one transfer. Source-path retention of three originals is an explicitly allowed Design choice, with historical status and source-resolved navigation outside unchanged bytes. The plan does not use an archive filename as an operational replacement or allow a mapped rule to survive only in historical prose. Changes to approved engineering meaning return to Design and reassessment.

The rollback units preserve source truth and coupled consumers; failed evidence and old judgments remain intact. M1 may be retained during M2 rollback only after independent assessment of compatibility with restored authority. Completion claims cannot precede reviewed coherent adoption and distinct successful Verify. There is no unreviewed third pilot, schema, publishing step or global improvement enforcement.

## Requirement and proof assessment

| Scope | Allocated proof and assessment |
| --- | --- |
| SKL-SR-01 and 21–23: common ownership, exact source retirement and remainder | M2/TG-04 requires actionable rules with population, trigger, outcome and approved exception/supersession, including the previously deficient lint/enforcement rules. TG-05 checks byte-preserved originals, related links/diagrams, retained operational/current consumers and FU-015–018's 17 skills; TG-FINAL-01 tests combined ownership and candidate coexistence. |
| SKL-SR-02–07 and 12–15: purpose, structure, specialist authority, portability, evidence, assets and bounded checks | M1/TG-01 independently assesses ordinary and triggered procedures/artifacts, author/reviewer separation and honest claims. TG-02/03 preserve validator and candidate behavior; M2/TG-04 transfers the exact common definitions and evaluates obsolete literal-source assertions before replacement. |
| SKL-SR-08–11 and 20: resource completeness, identity, transformations, fallback and consumers | TG-02 observes missing/malformed/unreadable/escaped/unknown selected resources, missing body triggers and unrelated-text bypass rejection. TG-03 compares full mapped resources and transformations across all supported candidates, including missing/stale rejection and unchanged inventory. TG-01 distinguishes runtime missing-method or authority stops from untriggered runtime use; TG-04 explicitly preserves convenience fallback versus package validity. |
| SKL-SR-16–19: useful bounded pilot improvement | TG-01 requires baseline-relative source/artifact walkthroughs for portable/governed authoring and advisory/formal review, malformed signals, late durable triggers and required stops. Actual loaded instructions and outputs/stops support independent usefulness judgment; a shorter body, audit or keyword pass cannot satisfy completion. Unfavorable/inconclusive results must be owned before M2 relies on them. |
| Composed risks and final closeout | TG-FINAL-01 follows final candidate author/reviewer paths with resources/assets and common-source provenance, retains negative transitive/heading-bypass cases, and checks final current consumers. The separate final whole-change Code Review checkpoint follows both milestones and corrections and precedes distinct Verify. Earlier milestone approval and integrated tests cannot replace it. |

All eight Design dimensions have an observable allocation: input classification and environment stops in TG-01; lifecycle/authority distinctions in TG-01/04/05; composition in TG-02/03 and TG-FINAL-01; late-trigger ordering and complete conflict/recovery procedure in M1/TG-01 with stale identity rejection in TG-03; missing-resource/fallback failures in TG-01/02/04; and migration/non-pilot coexistence in TG-03/04/05. The CLI's unchanged transaction implementation is not reimplemented or assigned a new universal concurrency benchmark. The relocation must still expose its complete current procedure, and any changed underlying behavior returns to its owner.

The verification groups use distinct observable failures rather than test counts or implementation-shaped success assertions. Production validation selection is exercised, not merely its helper. Test maintenance requires equivalent useful protection before retiring obsolete source-wording oracles, with unrelated historical fixtures retained. Integrated proof observes the full affected boundary, not a Cartesian scenario catalogue or universal agent-quality claim.

## Command feasibility and evidence limits

Read-only source inspection confirmed the named validator, generation, archive and guide-consumer entrypoints. The skill tests use unittest.main, so the planned -k targeted filter is supported; the plan correctly requires a nonzero selected count and additional explicit negative-case selection. build-adapters.py accepts --version and --output-dir, validate-adapters.py accepts --adapter-root, and v0.5.1 is the current manifest/default candidate version. ci.sh supports local mode and repeated explicit --path selection, which the plan requires when discovery needs it. The guide validator currently includes Skill Contract in its current-authority surfaces, supporting the bounded M2 correction and regression allocation.

Actually performed: read-only cat/sed/rg inspection; primary full scoped context; subject inspect --content full --max-bytes 8388608 for 49 subjects; comparison against upstream reviewed identities; review record --help; and targeted review recording. A search also named nonexistent scripts/ci.py; its error was observed and inspection used the actual scripts/ci.sh entrypoint. No conclusion depends on a nonexistent command or file.

The inspected plan-authoring check records passing prose, readability, link and whitespace checks with 53 advisory readability warnings. Those checks establish authoring hygiene, not semantic Delivery adequacy. This reviewer did not execute implementation tests, candidate generation or CI, and does not claim they pass. The plan allocates those actual runs and their limitations at the appropriate milestones. Earlier proof reuse requires an affirmative unchanged-subject/environment basis; fresh final whole-change review is mandatory regardless.
